To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the zero-bias peak in d-wave systems splits in magnetic field and the splitting obeys the universal relation delta ~ (B0)^(1/2), where the proportionality factor depends only on the strip width and the temperature, but not on the material.

the universal relation delta ~ (B/Bc2)^(1/2), where delta is the splitting of the zero-bias conductances peak and B is the magnetic field, is explained by long-ranged current flow from vortices in the sample, that the splitting is not related to the superconducting gap, and that the splitting is related to the current flow in the sample and not to the magnetic field.

a universal relation delta ~B^(1/2), with delta being the zero-bias conductances peak splitting and B the applied magnetic field, is derived analyticaly for d-wave superconductivity based on Abrikosov vortex currents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the magnetic field dependence of the zero-bias conductances in d-wave superconductor/normal metal hybrid structures.
the zero-bias conductive peak in d-wave high-Tc superconductors in a magnetic field.
the zero-bias conductace peak in d-wave systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed universal relation is a consequence of the long-ranged currents in d-wave superconductor samples, which is in full agreement both with experiment and theory.
the zero-bias conductances are determined by the magnetic flux through the sample.

the zero-bias conductances of d-wave superconducting strips are split in a universal way in an applied magnetic fields, which is caused by the long-ranged currents induced by Abrikosov flux vortices inside a strip.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the universal relation is not an indication for a new order parameter, but a consequence of the long-ranged vortex-current contributions in the sample.
the zero-bias conductances of d-wave superconducting strips are determined by the long-ranged currents of vortices in the sample.
the zero-bias peak splitting is due to long-ranged current flow from the vortex core to the sample edges.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the zero-bias conductances are sensitive to the magnetic flux inside the sample, and that the magnetic flux is not necessarily a measure for the magnetic field.
the zero-bias conductace peak splitting is not a direct measure of the magnetic penetration depth.

the universal relation delta ~ (B0)^(1/2), where delta is the peak separation, is an intrinsic property of the superconducting state, independent of the sample shape and the applied magnetic field geometry.
